title: First-Seen Record Deduper
prompt:
Implement `find_duplicate_indices(records) -> list[int]`. `records` is an ordered iterable of dictionaries. Process records from left to right. A record is a duplicate when any present `(field_name, value)` pair has already been claimed by an earlier non-duplicate record. Return the zero-based positions of duplicate records.

Claims are scoped to a field name: the same value in two different fields is not a conflict. Before accepting a record, check all of its present fields. If it is a duplicate, do not claim any of its other values. Missing fields are ignored. Compare provided values exactly; callers are responsible for any email, phone, whitespace, or case normalization.

Support arbitrary field sets without special-casing field names.

example.reasoning: The second record repeats a claimed phone value and the third repeats a claimed email value.
